subject: Information Theory
title: Data Brokers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Data Brokers.

hook.text: A company you've never heard of knows your income, health, and politics. Data brokers sell billions of profiles.

buildup.text: Data brokers aggregate info from public records, purchases, apps, and social media into detailed consumer profiles.

discovery.text: These profiles are sold to advertisers, insurers, employers, and political campaigns. Your data has a market price.

twist.text: You can't easily opt out. Your data is inferred from patterns even without consent. Correlation recreates your profile.

climax.text: Information theory explains: even seemingly anonymous data can be de-anonymized by cross-referencing enough datasets.

punchline.text: Strangers sell your secrets. You never signed up for it.

quiz.question: Why is opting out of data brokerage difficult?
options: Patterns and correlations can reconstruct profiles from other data
